post.description:
**Start here.** Public route.

**Scenario:** an ADMIN or EMPLOYEE signs in. The response holds a 15-minute `accessToken` (a JWT carrying `companyId`, `role` and `permissions`) and a 30-day single-use `refreshToken`. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on every other call.

**Rules:** the same message is returned for an unknown email and a wrong password. A deactivated account is refused. More than 5 attempts per minute from one IP for one email returns 429.

**Web (cookie mode):** send the header `X-Auth-Mode: cookie`. The response then sets `cp_access` and `cp_refresh` as HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies and returns `{ user, csrfToken }` with no tokens in the body.

parameters.description: Web clients send `cookie`: the tokens are then set as HttpOnly cookies (`cp_access`, `cp_refresh`) and left out of the response body, which carries a `csrfToken` instead. Leave it out for the bearer flow (mobile, Apidog, curl).

post.description:
Public route (the refresh token is the credential).

**Scenario:** the access token expired (401). Send the refresh token, store BOTH new tokens, and discard the old refresh token: it is single-use.

**Theft detection:** if an already-used refresh token is presented again, the whole session family is revoked and this returns 401. The new access token always carries the account's own company; a refresh can never change company.

**Web (cookie mode):** send `X-Auth-Mode: cookie` and no body. The refresh token is read from the `cp_refresh` cookie, both cookies are replaced, and the body holds the new `csrfToken`.

info.title: CheckPoint API
info.description:
Attendance, points and incentive payroll for companies. Every company's data is isolated.

## Quick start (2 minutes)
1. **Sign in:** `POST /api/auth/login` with the development admin `admin@checkpoint.local` / `AdminPassword123!` (created by `npx prisma db seed`).
2. **Authorize:** click **Authorize** (top right) and paste the `accessToken`. It is valid 15 minutes.
3. **Try routes:** `GET /api/auth/me`, then `POST /api/admin/invitations`, `GET /api/admin/shifts`, `POST /api/admin/attendance/corrections`, `GET /api/admin/audit-events`, and so on.
4. **Token expired (401)?** `POST /api/auth/refresh` with your `refreshToken`, and keep the NEW pair (refresh tokens are single-use).

The full step-by-step cycle with real request and response bodies is in `docs/10-API_TESTING_GUIDE.md`.

## Rules that apply everywhere
- **Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` (mobile, tools). Web clients send `X-Auth-Mode: cookie` on login, refresh and logout and get `HttpOnly` cookies instead; a write authenticated by cookie must also send `X-CSRF-Token`. When both a header and a cookie arrive, the header wins. Only login, refresh, logout and invitation accept are public.
- **Company scope:** your company comes from your token, never from the request. A record of another company answers **404**, the same as a missing one.
- **Roles:** ADMIN may use the `/admin/*` routes; EMPLOYEE gets **403** there. Employees reach only their own data (`/me/*`).
- **Validation:** unknown properties in a body are rejected with **400**.
- **Errors** always look like `{ "statusCode": 404, "message": "...", "error": "Not Found" }`.
- **Money** is EGP. Amounts come back as strings (for example `"12000"`).

cookie-auth.name: cp_access
cookie-auth.description: Web clients only: set by POST /api/auth/login with the header X-Auth-Mode: cookie

actorUserId.description: Who did it; null for system events

changes.description: What changed. Never contains passwords or tokens.

example: Must be a valid email address
message.description: A message, or a list of validation messages (400)

error.description: HTTP status text (absent on some errors)

fullName.description: From the employee record; null if the account has none

mustChangePassword.description: True for a first-time or reset password (not enforced yet)

accessToken.description: JWT, valid 15 minutes. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

refreshToken.description: Opaque single-use token, valid 30 days. Exchange it at POST /auth/refresh.

csrfToken.description: Send it back as the `X-CSRF-Token` header on every POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE while signed in by cookie.

refreshToken.description: The NEW refresh token. The one you sent is now spent; keep only this one.

csrfToken.description: The new CSRF token for the new access cookie. Replace the old one.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token returned by login or by the previous refresh. Single-use. Required, except in cookie mode (header `X-Auth-Mode: cookie`), where it is read from the `cp_refresh` cookie.

companyId.description: The caller's company. Taken from the token, never from the request.

mustChangePassword.description: True until the user changes the one-time password; every route except PATCH /me/password, GET /auth/me and logout answers 403 meanwhile

csrfToken.description: Only when the request was authenticated by the access cookie: the token to send as `X-CSRF-Token`. Use it to recover after a page reload.

message.example: Access granted: you have users.read permission

active.description: false deactivates the user and revokes all their refresh tokens at once; true reactivates

email.description: Login email. Unique across the whole system.

password.description: Initial password (stored as an argon2id hash)

employeeCode.description: Employee number. Unique within the company.

initialSalary.description: Monthly salary in EGP, effective from the 1st of the current month

currency.description: EGP is the only supported currency

amount.description: Decimal amount, serialized as a string to avoid rounding

activeFrom.description: First date an absence (BLACK) may be recorded

disabledAt.description: Set when the user is deactivated

currentSalary.description: The salary in force today (Cairo date): the latest version that has already started. null if none has started.

upcomingSalary.description: The next salary, dated in the future, or null. It never counts as current before its date.

upcomingSalary.description: The next salary, dated in the future, or null. It never counts as current before its date.

salaries.description: Full salary history, newest first. Only on GET /admin/users/{id}.

password.description: One-time password the Admin hands to the user; they must replace it at first sign-in.

mustChangePassword.description: Always true: the user must set their own password next.

currency.description: EGP is the only supported currency

effectiveFrom.description: Must be the 1st of a month. Past months are never rewritten; use a new date.

newPassword.description: The new password. Must differ from the current one.

message.example: Password changed. Please sign in again.

email.description: Email of the person being invited. Must not have an account yet.

employeeCode.description: Employee number to assign. Unique within the company.

token.description: The one-time token. Returned ONLY here and never stored: share it with the invitee now.

invitationLink.description: The accept link (INVITE_URL_BASE + token). Share it yourself when `emailSent` is false.

emailSent.description: True only when SMTP is configured and the email was handed to it.

token.description: The one-time token the Admin shared with the invitee

message.example: Account created. You can now sign in.

description.example: Please arrive early to help with opening.

allEmployees.description: When true, all current and future employees in the company can see this offer.

active.description: The location is deactivated; its row and assignments remain.
Set false to deactivate, or true to reactivate the location.

locationIds.description: The complete new set; an empty list removes every assignment.

accuracy.description: GPS accuracy radius in meters; must not exceed the company's gps_max_accuracy_m.

overtimeGreens.description: Overtime GREEN points awarded (whole hours after the shift end).

days.description: Days with no attendance expected; at least one day must remain a working day.
